verdict_text: NO. The second task vector is taken against the partially merged tensor instead of the unmodified base: the script computes `tmp = b + λ(f1 - b)` and then `tmp + λ(f2 - tmp)`, which expands to `b + λ(f1-b) + λ(f2-b) - λ²(f1-b)`, an extra `-0.16·(ft1 - base)` term. This violates Required result step 2, which requires `out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X] - base[X]) + λ(ft2[X] - base[X])` with each task vector measured against the original base (the exact ordering hazard the Objective warns about). The deviation is proportional to the fine-tune delta itself, so it will generally exceed the 1e-3 relative Frobenius tolerance on the 64 merged tensors. The verification, counts, and unchanged-tensor handling are otherwise correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
